purpose: Cobimetinib is used to treat a type of skin cancer called melanoma that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is specifically used in patients whose cancer has a certain gene change called a BRAF mutation. It is always used together with another medicine called vemurafenib to help fight the cancer more effectively.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes have faulty signals that tell them to grow out of control. Cobimetinib works by blocking a specific protein called MEK, which is part of that faulty signaling pathway. By blocking MEK, this medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and rash are very common. You may also notice tiredness, swelling in your arms or legs, fever, and sensitivity to sunlight. Some people experience vision changes or muscle pain as well.
warnings: Cobimetinib can cause serious bleeding, including in the brain or stomach, so tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bleeding. It can also cause serious heart problems, liver damage, serious skin reactions, and eye problems — your doctor will monitor you closely with regular tests. Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen daily. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby, and use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 60 mg (three 20 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day for 21 days in a row, followed by 7 days off. This 28-day cycle is then repeated. It can be taken with or without food. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not skip doses.
